content:
Looking at the LLM working on the proofs, it seems like much time is spent on figuring out which module to import to give definitions and instances.

For example, “which module should be imported to fix the error

failed to synthesize instance of type class
  Fintype (Fin 3)

?” (the LLM eventually solve this, answer is

import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Fin

, but only after 3–4 tool calls.

Is this a solved problem? e.g. if there's a tool that magically find and add imports as needed, it suffice to tell the agent “run tool X before each build”. If anything, human is probably slower than LLM to figure these things out, so I'd expect it to be solved way before agent era.

(apparently, bare import Mathlib gives a hard compile error of missing .lean file or something. It seems like the LLM expects this to be blanket import everything…?)

Unfortunately this is not really a solved problem! So we should solve it. :-)

Note that there is an automatic code action associated to all unknownIdentifier messages https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Error-Explanations/About___--unknownIdentifier/ that is very helpful.

However an agent just running lake build won't see this. I'm not sure what the right mechanism is here.

We could encourage agents to just use import Mathlib, and then either run lake shake or #min_imports in ... or #import_bumps afterwards, but both are awkward. (This would help address the "failed to synthesize" problems as well.)

Could you explain in what situation you're seeing an error from import Mathlib?)

I think the compiler says something about missing olean file, which neither I nor the agent have really debugged why. Will figure out one day.
If there's some way to get useful result over LSP or whatever, it should only take a bit of wrapper code to feed that to the agent. May not be as bad as it sounds.
I always develop with import Mathlib in FLT (because I'm worried about missing instances) and squeeze at the end
